question: How does occupational health nursing mostly differ from regular hospital nursing?

options.A: Prevention of workplace injuries and illnesses
options.C: Managing chronic diseases in elderly communities

explanation: Spot on! While hospitals focus heavily on treating sick patients, occupational health nurses stop injuries and illnesses before they even happen on the job.

question: Why must an occupational health nurse team up with safety officers and management?

options.A: To manage the daily production schedule of the factory floor
options.B: To audit financial records for the company's medical insurance
options.C: To handle legal lawsuits filed against injured employees
options.D: To ensure working conditions meet acceptable health standards

explanation: You got it! Working hand-in-hand with safety teams helps the nurse keep the work environment safe and healthy for everyone.

question: What is a main duty of an occupational health nurse working as a case manager?

options.A: Conducting annual financial audits for human resources
options.B: Designing new production machinery to eliminate safety hazards
options.C: Coordinating medical treatments and return-to-work plans for injured staff
options.D: Purchasing personal protective equipment for the entire industrial plant

explanation: Exactly! As case managers, nurses guide injured workers through their recovery and help them safely get back to work.

question: A worker comes to you feeling very stressed and slightly depressed about personal issues, which is affecting their work. By listening and guiding them, what role are you playing?
explanation: Well done! Offering a listening ear and confidential advice for stress or personal worries falls right under the counselor role.

question: Which major Nigerian law covers factory ventilation, lighting, and general worker welfare?
explanation: Correct! The Factories Act is the key Nigerian law that sets the rules for factory safety and worker welfare.

question: A nurse thinks safety rules only matter in big factories and ignores small offices in the building. Where is the mistake in this thinking?

options.A: Nursing councils have no say over non-manufacturing environments
options.B: Administrative offices are completely exempt from all laws
options.C: Workplace safety regulations extend to offices and small-scale enterprises as well
options.D: Only human resources are responsible for office building safety

explanation: Spot on! Safety laws apply everywhere people work—even in small offices, not just heavy industries.

question: Which of these is considered a physical workplace hazard?
explanation: You nailed it! Physical hazards include things like loud noise, extreme temperatures, and vibrations that can wear down your health over time.

question: Why are regular walkthrough inspections so important for an occupational health nurse?

options.A: To discipline workers who fail to wear proper uniforms
options.B: To check the financial profits of the plant
options.C: To replace safety officers during their annual leave
options.D: To observe daily work tasks and identify unaddressed environmental risks

explanation: Exactly! Walking through the workspace lets you spot hidden dangers that workers might just get used to and forget to report.

question: What is the main reason for doing a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To test physical strength for office roles
options.C: To provide immediate treatment for interview injuries
options.D: To establish a baseline health status before a worker begins a job

explanation: Correct! Pre-placement exams give you a clear starting point of the worker's health so you can notice if the job affects them later.

question: Why would an occupational health nurse schedule regular hearing (audiometric) tests for factory workers?

options.A: To evaluate stress from night shift rotations
options.B: To detect early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it becomes permanent
options.C: To measure lung capacity after chemical dust exposure
options.D: To screen for bloodborne infections from shared gear

explanation: Spot on! Regular hearing tests help catch any hearing damage early on, before it turns into permanent deafness.

question: What is the very first thing an occupational health nurse should do when an injury happens at work?

options.A: File a lawsuit against the company owner
options.B: Calculate financial compensation for the worker
options.C: Assess the injury and provide immediate first aid
options.D: Conduct a drug test on all witnesses

explanation: You got it! First things first: always check the victim and give prompt first aid or stabilization before worrying about anything else.

question: Why do workers sometimes hide minor injuries instead of visiting the clinic?

options.A: Not knowing the clinic is open in the mornings
options.B: Fear of losing pay or facing disciplinary action from management
options.C: Thinking safety nurses only handle major surgeries
options.D: Preferring traditional herbs for all injuries

explanation: Sad but true—many workers worry they will get punished, lose wages, or risk their jobs if they report small accidents.

question: What is the main goal of ergonomics in the workplace?

options.A: Inspecting the concrete strength of the building
options.B: Setting exact employee salaries and bonuses
options.C: Fitting workstations and tools to match human body limits
options.D: Managing the menu in the staff cafeteria

explanation: Exactly! Ergonomics is all about designing work tools and chairs to fit the human body, preventing physical strain.

question: Which health problem is most often caused by poor ergonomic design at work?

options.B: Hereditary blood disorders and sickle cell crises
options.C: Musculoskeletal disorders and chronic back pain
options.D: Acute viral gastroenteritis and food poisoning

explanation: Well done! Bad chairs and poorly arranged desks force awkward postures, leading directly to backaches and muscle strains.

question: What is a major ethical dilemma an occupational health nurse frequently faces?

options.A: Deciding whether to do surgery without a doctor
options.B: Balancing loyalty to the employer with the duty to protect worker health and privacy
options.C: Choosing between clinical nursing and selling products
options.D: Reporting fellow nurses to criminal courts for minor errors

explanation: Spot on! Because the company pays your salary but nursing ethics demand patient privacy, it can be a tough tightrope to walk.

question: An employer demands to see the full medical diagnosis and lab results of a worker who visited your clinic. What are you ethically allowed to share?

options.A: The complete confidential medical history and psychiatric notes
options.B: Only the worker's fitness-for-work status and necessary job accommodations
options.D: Detailed lab test values and family health records

explanation: You nailed it! To keep trust and protect privacy, you only tell the boss if the worker is fit for duty or needs special adjustments—keep the private diagnosis to yourself.
